blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence: - A plugin system for export formats, so that PDF, XLSX, XML and JSON exports can be added later by dropping a module in `src/export/plugins/`.
findings.recommendation: The Why only asks to stop copying invoices one by one into a spreadsheet ("Accountants copy invoices one by one into their spreadsheet at the end of each month."); a CSV export answers it. No PDF, XLSX, XML or JSON export is requested. Drop the plugin system from What Changes and Impact (`src/export/` can shrink to one CSV module), replace the design's "Decision: Exports go through a plugin registry" with a single CSV function — the alternative it rejected only as "not extensible" — and remove task 1.2 ("Plugin registry discovering `src/export/plugins/`"). Add the registry in the change that brings a second format.
findings.title: Plugin system for future export formats nobody asked for

findings.evidence: The settings page SHALL let a user choose their preferred export format among the installed plugins.
findings.location: specs/invoice-export/spec.md#Requirement: Users choose their export format
findings.recommendation: With CSV as the only format, a choice of format has nothing to choose between, and the Why says nothing about preferences. Remove this requirement and its scenarios, the What Changes bullet "A settings page where each user picks their preferred export format.", `web/src/settings/` from Impact, the last sentence of the design decision ("A settings page stores each user's preferred format.") and task 2.1. As written the requirement is also unverifiable: "exports use CSV" cannot be told apart from the default when CSV is the only format, and it needs a stored per-user preference the plan never places anywhere.
findings.title: Per-user export-format preference on the settings page nobody asked for

findings.recommendation: `GET /invoices.csv?month=YYYY-MM` is a new input-taking route that returns every invoice of a month with its customer, yet no domain is ticked, so no expert reviews who may call it or what customer data leaves the system; the spec has no unauthorized-caller scenario. Tick `security` and `personal-data` (or write the reason on each line if they do not apply). If the settings page stays despite R-skeptic-2, tick `user-interface` too.
findings.title: New invoice endpoint exposes customer data with security and personal-data unticked
